phase_0.boundary_condition: The structural enforcement of a single-axis chiral configuration that persists across interaction events, defining the scope of the fee as a localized transaction cost.

⊢.justification: The state before the fee is instantiated; no scalar value exists, no transactional relationship is defined, and the chiral axis is unmarked.

⊣.justification: The closed boundary that contains the fee's structural definition; the point where the chiral memory depth n is fixed and the transactional scope is sealed.

≻.justification: The directed morphism where the scalar fee value moves from the payer to the payee, establishing the transactional flow.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism that inverts the signed direction of the chiral axis, distinguishing the donating pole from the accepting pole.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of fee events where one transaction follows another, maintaining the localized nature of the cost.

⊙.justification: The identity state where the fee recognizes itself as the cost of its own existence; the transaction is the record of the transaction.

∈.justification: The split into two arms: the affirmative arm where the fee is paid and the negative arm where the fee is refused or fails to materialize.

∋.justification: The rejoining of the paid and refused arms into a single verdict; if both states hold (paid and refused), the result is a paradice (B).

⊤.justification: The constructive proof that the fee has been successfully transferred and the transactional relationship is established.

⊥.justification: The constructive refutation that the fee was not paid, the transaction failed, or the chiral axis was not engaged.

⊞.justification: The state where the fee is both paid and refused simultaneously; a paradice where the transactional relationship holds both truth and falsity without collapse.

⊡.justification: The permanent, append-only record of the fee transaction; once fixed, the chiral memory and transactional cost cannot be undone.

phase_3.void_description: No fee exists; the transactional relationship is undefined and the chiral axis is unmarked.
phase_3.true_description: The fee is affirmed; the transaction is complete and the chiral memory is established.
phase_3.false_description: The fee is refuted; the transaction failed and the chiral axis remains unengaged.
phase_3.both_description: The fee is both paid and refused; a paradice where the transactional relationship holds contradictory states simultaneously.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the pre-transactional void where no fee exists and the chiral axis is unmarked.
Fork the pending fee transaction into two arms: the affirmative arm (fee paid) and the negative arm (fee refused).
On the affirmative arm, execute the forward morphism of the payer-to-payee transfer.
Affirm the fee on the affirmative arm; the transaction is constructively proven.
On the negative arm, execute the reverse morphism of the chiral parity flip.
Refute the fee on the negative arm; the transaction is constructively refuted.
Hold the paradice state where the fee is both paid and refused simultaneously.
Rejoin the affirmative and negative arms into a single resolved transactional state.
Chain the resolved transaction to the next fee event in the sequence.
Establish the self-referential identity of the fee as the cost of its own existence.
Fix the transactional record as an immutable ledger entry.
Seal the enforced chiral boundary that contains the fee's structural definition.

phase_5.alfs_store: The immutable ledger (IFIX) that serves as the canonical reference for all fee transactions.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The scalar fee value consumed per transaction cycle.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The pending fee transaction with undefined chiral axis.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The resolved transactional state with fixed chiral memory.
